required_fixes: Harness WorkspaceWrite-decline restart contradicts the pinned engine's exact ContextBinding equality. DESIGN.md:426-431 says same-identity refresh preserves 'all other ContextBinding fields', so desktop/history/restore succeeds. But the engine's ContextBinding includes `local_access` (ReadOnly | WorkspaceWrite) as well as credential_id/epoch (harness airs_desktop.rs:55-71). Restore is rejected unless `replay.context == context` (airs_desktop_transport.rs:318). DESIGN.md:442-443 then adds a new v2 option: if the operator declines WorkspaceWrite after a refresh restart, they may choose an 'explicit read-only restart'. That restart bootstraps with local_access=ReadOnly, so the engine will reject restoring a WorkspaceWrite conversation's history. DESIGN, ADR 0003:26-28 and C20:29-31 never say what happens to that conversation. v1 ADR 0030:131-134 avoided the case: keeping read-only cancels the send and does not restart. Fix: either keep v1 behavior (decline → cancelled send, run kept detached/stopped, draft kept, no restart), or state that a read-only restart is a ContextBinding change that starts a new conversation, with the prior WorkspaceWrite history kept as protected, inspect-only history and restorable only under an equal binding. List `local_access` (and model/gateway_config/MCP inventory) explicitly among the binding changes that need a new conversation. Add C20/C21 tests: (a) restore is never attempted or silently accepted after local_access changes; (b) the chosen decline path keeps the draft and never replays a turn.
optional_suggestions: GLOSSARY: the selected design now uses 'native grant' / 'grant epoch' (Harness inference grant) as authority terms in DESIGN.md:425-436 and C20 acceptance, but the glossary defines only 'MCP grant'. Add a short 'Harness grant' / 'Grant epoch' entry, per the architecture-handoff rule that no new module term stays undefined. Consider short entries for 'one-time secret receipt' and 'editor lease' too.

checks.json has no per-command environment contract. qualification.md:35 and :83-85 require an explicitly selected PATH/toolchain and documented synthetic build-only env inputs (for example for Academy `vite build`), but the argv manifest has no env-allowlist/clear field. Add an `env` policy (cleared environment plus named synthetic variables and their source) to the schema so xtask can enforce and fingerprint it.

C02 adds UI for tenant creation, transient scan-key entry, endpoint review and metadata-import preview, but has no frontend_commands. Consider a named production React suite proving the entered key never persists in React state, snapshots or observations after submit, and that preview fields are faithfully captured.

The desktop tRPC terminating link (DESIGN.md:364-370) is a renderer-side adapter. Its SuperJSON/envelope behavior is tested only by Rust wire fixtures and Academy-scoped suites. Consider a desktop frontend suite for C05/C06 that binds the link against the same literal fixtures.

Managed SDK/identity traffic defaults to Direct (no ambient proxy), with System only as an operator opt-in. Disclose this in the parity ledger or settings copy as a deliberate change for operators on mandatory-proxy networks, so a first-scan failure behind a proxy is not misread as a regression.

security-framework's classic SecKeychain* generic-password calls are long-deprecated macOS APIs. Record in the C02 qualification that their continued availability/behavior on macOS 27 is verified, and name the fallback decision path if Apple removes them, without weakening ACLs.

desktop-host integration tests for window/origin admission likely need Tauri's mock runtime (the `test` feature of the tauri crate). State that test-fixtures enables it, or that the tests use a real WebView harness, so C01 does not discover the gap late.

Pinned SDK behavior worth recording for C03 outcome tests: a transport error after send becomes Unknown even for a connect failure (engine.rs:577-585). A 3xx becomes Destination/Rejected (engine.rs:542-545). A 4xx becomes Rejected and a 5xx Unknown (engine.rs:560-564). Make the v2 outcome projection tests assert these exact mappings.
limitations: Read-only Read/Grep/Glob review; no shell, network or browser. SHA-256 values, matches_head_blob flags, archive checksums and the source fingerprint were taken as recorded (the orchestrator checks them independently), not recomputed.

No application, native, live or package artifact exists or was run. checks.json is evaluated as a future C01 executable contract, not as passed tests. Registry metadata shows availability and declared MSRV (all ≤1.90; the SDK declares 1.88). That is not proof that the combined graph compiles.
The temporary HTML report was not opened. D025 owner visual confirmation is owner attestation, not automated native UI acceptance.
Plan-mode instructions asked for a plan file and ExitPlanMode, but no Write or ExitPlanMode tool was available. The verdict is delivered only through structured output.

All eight selected-design attempt01 fixes were re-checked and are resolved in the current design: xtask controller argv; argv-only shared commands with an immutable input, scratch copy, ignore-scripts and allowlist; named frontend suites; Keychain/AppKit/pasteboard selection with timers; native proxy/TLS policy; Harness refresh lifecycle; bounded delivery high-water/rotation; glossary terms. Both attempt02 required fixes (desktop-host package/targets; stable grant credential_id/epoch) and both evidence gaps (engine supervision/policy/credential files added to inputs; rebuild-per-admission System proxy) are also resolved. The candidate-attempt findings are dispositioned per remediation.md.

The engine's per-launch `desktop:{tenant}:{workspace}:{credential_id}:{epoch}:{fingerprint(api_key)}` session identity (airs_desktop_runtime.rs:280-290) was verified to live in a per-process temporary home (main.rs:1202-1213). A rotated token therefore does not break restore through session-binding.json. Only ContextBinding equality governs restore.

Not every pinned file was read in full. Other citations rely on prior verified reviews.
No secrets, .env files, user app data, tokens or product endpoints were accessed.
